title: See the Rosetta Stone at the British Museum
description: Free, enormous, and impossible in one visit. Pick three galleries and ignore the rest, or you will see nothing properly.

title: Walk across the Thames on the Tower Bridge glass floor
description: The high walkways were closed for seventy years and reopened with a glass floor forty-two metres above the river.

title: Stand on the Prime Meridian at Greenwich
description: Longitude zero, and the room where the problem of finding it at sea was finally solved by Harrison's clocks.

title: Watch a play standing in the Globe yard
description: Five pounds to stand as a groundling in an open-roofed reconstruction, which is how the plays were written to be watched.

title: Walk the whole of Hampstead Heath to Kenwood
description: Three hundred and twenty hectares of unmanicured London, with swimming ponds open all year and the best free view of the city from Parliament Hill.

title: Eat at Borough Market on a weekday
description: A thousand years of market on the same spot. Saturdays are unbearable; Tuesday lunchtime is the market the traders prefer.

title: Find Sir John Soane's house exactly as he left it
description: An architect's house kept by act of parliament in the arrangement he died with, crammed with sarcophagi and mirrors. Free, and tiny.

title: Ride the whole Elizabeth line end to end
description: Reading to Abbey Wood through tunnels bored under the entire city, past platforms that look like an airport of the near future.

title: Get inside the Stonehenge circle at sunrise
description: Stone circle access is booked separately and outside opening hours, which is the only way to stand among them rather than behind rope.

title: Explore Wells Cathedral and its scissor arches
description: Inverted arches added in 1338 to stop the tower sinking, and an astronomical clock whose jousting knights have run since 1390.

title: Walk the Cheddar Gorge clifftop circuit
description: The deepest gorge in Britain, with a five-kilometre loop along both rims and caves where the oldest complete British skeleton was found.

title: Walk the Jurassic Coast to Durdle Door
description: A limestone arch below a steep chalk path from Lulworth Cove. The whole coast reads as 185 million years laid out west to east.

title: Cross Dartmoor on a letterboxing walk
description: Hundreds of hidden stamp boxes scattered across the moor since 1854. Wild camping is legal here, which it is nowhere else in England.

title: Walk out to St Michael's Mount on the causeway
description: A tidal island with a castle, still lived in by the St Aubyn family. Walk out at low water and take the boat back.

title: See the biomes at the Eden Project
description: Two vast biome domes in a worked-out china clay pit, one rainforest, one Mediterranean. The rainforest canopy walkway is the bit to do.

title: Watch a play at the Minack Theatre
description: An open-air theatre cut into a granite cliff by one woman and her gardener from 1931 onwards, with the Atlantic as the backdrop.

title: Walk the white cliffs from Dover to South Foreland
description: Five kilometres of chalk clifftop to a Victorian lighthouse, with France visible on a clear day and peregrines on the face.

title: Watch seals at Blakeney Point
description: England's largest grey seal colony, with pups on the shingle from November. Boats run from Morston Quay on the tide.

title: See the Sutton Hoo ship burial site
description: The mounds where an Anglo-Saxon king was buried in a ship in the 620s, found in 1939 days before the war began.

title: Punt on the Cherwell in Oxford
description: Punting from the Cherwell Boathouse up past the Parks. Push off the bottom, do not let go of the pole, and expect to fall in once.

title: See the King's College chapel fan vault
description: The largest fan vault in the world, and the Christmas Eve carol service that the BBC has broadcast since 1928.

title: Swim on the rooftop at the Thermae Bath Spa
description: The only natural thermal water in Britain, in a Georgian city built entirely from the same honey-coloured stone.

title: Walk the best-preserved stretch of Hadrian's Wall
description: Steel Rigg to Housesteads runs along the crags where the wall still stands highest. Eighty Roman miles coast to coast if you want the lot.

title: Look up in the Northumberland dark sky park
description: The largest area of protected night sky in Europe, with an observatory in the forest and aurora on the better nights.

title: Cross the sands to Lindisfarne
description: A tidal causeway to Holy Island, with published safe crossing times and a refuge box for people who ignore them.

title: Walk the Malham Cove limestone pavement
description: A seventy-metre curved cliff with a field of clints and grikes on top, and peregrines nesting on the face in spring.

title: Ride the Settle to Carlisle railway
description: Seventy-two miles over the Ribblehead Viaduct and through Blea Moor, saved from closure by a public campaign in the 1980s.

title: Walk the Yorkshire Three Peaks in a day
description: Pen-y-ghent, Whernside and Ingleborough: 39 kilometres and 1,585 metres of ascent, traditionally inside twelve hours.

title: See Whitby Abbey above the harbour
description: The ruin Bram Stoker used for Dracula's landfall, reached by 199 steps from a town that still lands its own crab.

title: Ride the Blackpool heritage trams along the front
description: The oldest electric tramway in Britain, running since 1885, along seven miles of seafront and illuminations in autumn.

title: Row out to the island on Ullswater
description: The steamers have run since 1859. Take one to Howtown and walk the shore path back, which is the finest low-level walk in the Lakes.

title: Climb Scafell Pike from Wasdale
description: England's highest point at 978 metres, up from the deepest lake in the country. The Corridor Route is the interesting way.

title: Take the ferry across the Mersey
description: Fifty minutes on the river with the Three Graces on the skyline, and the song playing on the tannoy whether you want it or not.

title: Walk the Monsal Trail through the tunnels
description: Thirteen kilometres of former railway through four lit tunnels in the Peak District, flat enough for anyone and open to bikes.

title: Walk up Arthur's Seat before breakfast
description: An extinct volcano inside the city, 251 metres up, with the whole of Edinburgh and the Forth laid out at the top.

title: Find the closes off the Royal Mile
description: Narrow alleys running downhill off the spine of the old town, several of them buried under later buildings and open to tours.

title: Ride the Jacobite over the Glenfinnan Viaduct
description: A steam train from Fort William to Mallaig over the curved viaduct. Watching it from the hillside path is free and just as good.

title: Walk into Glen Coe on the Lost Valley path
description: A hanging valley the MacDonalds hid stolen cattle in, up a boulder scramble from the road. The massacre of 1692 happened below.

title: Climb Ben Nevis by the mountain track
description: Britain's highest at 1,345 metres. The summit plateau is in cloud most days and navigating off it has killed people; carry a compass.

title: Look for dolphins at Chanonry Point
description: Bottlenose dolphins feed in the narrows on a rising tide, close enough to the shingle spit to hear them breathe.

title: Walk the machair beaches of Harris
description: Luskentyre and Seilebost are white shell sand against turquoise water, and they are usually empty even in July.

title: Take a boat to Staffa and Fingal's Cave
description: Hexagonal basalt columns and a sea cave that gave Mendelssohn his overture. Puffins nest on the top in early summer.

title: Land on St Kilda
description: Forty miles beyond the Outer Hebrides, evacuated in 1930 and now the largest gannet colony in the North Atlantic. Weather cancels most trips.

title: Walk into the Neolithic village at Skara Brae
description: Older than the pyramids, with stone dressers and box beds still in place, uncovered by a storm in 1850.

title: Watch puffins at Sumburgh Head
description: Puffins nest within a few metres of the cliff path here from May to early August, which is unusually close for Britain.

title: Ride the funicular and walk the Cairngorm plateau
description: The largest area of arctic-alpine plateau in Britain, with reindeer, ptarmigan and weather that turns in minutes.

title: Kayak among the Slate Islands
description: Flooded slate quarries and the Corryvreckan whirlpool nearby, third largest in the world. Go with a guide for the tide.

title: Walk the Speyside whisky trail
description: Half of Scotland's distilleries in one river valley, linked by a walking route on an old railway line.

title: Walk a stage of the Pembrokeshire Coast Path
description: Two hundred and ninety kilometres around the only coastal national park in Britain, with more ascent overall than Everest.

title: Take the boat to Skomer for the puffins
description: Forty thousand puffins and the world's largest Manx shearwater colony. Landing numbers are capped; go on the first boat.

title: Ride the Ffestiniog narrow gauge railway
description: The oldest independent railway company in the world, built in 1836 to bring slate down to Porthmadog by gravity.

title: Cross the Devil's Bridge at the Aberglaslyn Pass
description: A river gorge path along an old railway ledge with chains bolted to the rock where the footing runs out.

title: Zip line over a slate quarry at Penrhyn
description: The fastest zip line in the world at over 160 kilometres an hour, strung across a working slate quarry.

title: Walk the walls of Conwy Castle town
description: Edward I's ring of castles, and the most complete set of medieval town walls in Britain still walkable end to end.

title: Walk the four waterfalls at Ystradfellte
description: You can walk behind Sgwd yr Eira, which drops over an overhang into a pool. The path is genuinely slippery all year.

title: Look for red kites at Bwlch Nant yr Arian
description: Red kites were down to a handful of Welsh pairs in the 1930s. A hundred and more now come in to feed here every afternoon.

title: Cross the Carrick-a-Rede rope bridge
description: A rope bridge thirty metres above the sea to a salmon fishermen's island. Timed tickets, and it closes in high wind.

title: Walk the Dark Hedges avenue
description: A beech avenue planted in the eighteenth century, now closed to traffic after too many people stopped in the middle of the road.

title: Walk the Mourne Wall in the Mournes
description: Thirty-five kilometres of drystone wall built over the summits between 1904 and 1922 to enclose a reservoir catchment.

title: Go underground at Marble Arch Caves
description: A show cave you enter partly by boat, on a global geopark that crosses the border into Cavan.
